<file>
00001| ---
00002| title: cacheTag
00003| description: Learn how to use the cacheTag function to manage cache invalidation in your Next.js application.
00004| related:
00005|   title: Related
00006|   description: View related API references.
00007|   links:
00008|     - app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents
00009|     - app/api-reference/directives/use-cache
00010|     - app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag
00011|     - app/api-reference/functions/updateTag
00012|     - app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife
00013| ---
00014| 
00015| The `cacheTag` function allows you to tag cached data for on-demand invalidation. By associating tags with cache entries, you can selectively purge or revalidate specific cache entries without affecting other cached data.
00016| 
00017| ## Usage
00018| 
00019| To use `cacheTag`, enable the [`cacheComponents` flag](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) in your `next.config.js` file:
00020| 
00021| ```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher
00022| import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
00023| 
00024| const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
00025|   cacheComponents: true,
00026| }
00027| 
00028| export default nextConfig
00029| ```
00030| 
00031| ```js filename="next.config.js" switcher
00032| const nextConfig = {
00033|   cacheComponents: true,
00034| }
00035| 
00036| export default nextConfig
00037| ```
00038| 
00039| The `cacheTag` function takes one or more string values.
00040| 
00041| ```tsx filename="app/data.ts" switcher
00042| import { cacheTag } from 'next/cache'
00043| 
00044| export async function getData() {
00045|   'use cache'
00046|   cacheTag('my-data')
00047|   const data = await fetch('/api/data')
00048|   return data
00049| }
00050| ```
00051| 
00052| ```jsx filename="app/data.js" switcher
00053| import { cacheTag } from 'next/cache'
00054| 
00055| export async function getData() {
00056|   'use cache'
00057|   cacheTag('my-data')
00058|   const data = await fetch('/api/data')
00059|   return data
00060| }
00061| ```
00062| 
00063| You can then purge the cache on-demand from a [Server Function](/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data) or [Route Handler](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route):
00064| 
00065| - Use [`updateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/updateTag) for read-your-own-writes scenarios, such as forms and other user-triggered mutations, where a user makes a change and the next read should fetch fresh data immediately. `updateTag` is only available inside Server Functions.
00066| - Use [`revalidateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag) when it is acceptable to serve stale data while revalidation happens in the background, or when revalidating from a [Route Handler](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route) or other context.
00067| 
00068| For example, this Server Function adds a post and then purges every cache entry tagged `'my-data'` so the next read reflects the change:
00069| 
00070| ```tsx filename="app/action.ts" switcher
00071| 'use server'
00072| 
00073| import { updateTag } from 'next/cache'
00074| 
00075| export default async function submit() {
00076|   await addPost()
00077|   updateTag('my-data')
00078| }
00079| ```
00080| 
00081| ```jsx filename="app/action.js" switcher
00082| 'use server'
00083| 
00084| import { updateTag } from 'next/cache'
00085| 
00086| export default async function submit() {
00087|   await addPost()
00088|   updateTag('my-data')
00089| }
00090| ```
00091| 
00092| ## Good to know
00093| 
00094| - **Idempotent Tags**: Applying the same tag multiple times has no additional effect.
00095| - **Multiple Tags**: You can assign multiple tags to a single cache entry by passing multiple string values to `cacheTag`.
00096| 
00097| ```tsx
00098| cacheTag('tag-one', 'tag-two')
00099| ```
00100| 
00101| - **Limits**: A single `cacheTag()` call accepts up to 128 tags, each with a maximum length of 256 characters. Tags longer than 256 characters are skipped, and any tags past the 128th in one call are dropped. Both cases log a console warning.
00102| 
00103| ## Examples
00104| 
00105| ### Tagging components or functions
00106| 
00107| Tag your cached data by calling `cacheTag` within a cached function or component:
00108| 
00109| ```tsx filename="app/components/bookings.tsx" switcher
00110| import { cacheTag } from 'next/cache'
00111| 
00112| interface BookingsProps {
00113|   type: string
00114| }
00115| 
00116| export async function Bookings({ type = 'haircut' }: BookingsProps) {
00117|   'use cache'
00118|   cacheTag('bookings-data')
00119| 
00120|   async function getBookingsData() {
00121|     const data = await fetch(`/api/bookings?type=${encodeURIComponent(type)}`)
00122|     return data
00123|   }
00124| 
00125|   return //...
00126| }
00127| ```
00128| 
00129| ```jsx filename="app/components/bookings.js" switcher
00130| import { cacheTag } from 'next/cache'
00131| 
00132| export async function Bookings({ type = 'haircut' }) {
00133|   'use cache'
00134|   cacheTag('bookings-data')
00135| 
00136|   async function getBookingsData() {
00137|     const data = await fetch(`/api/bookings?type=${encodeURIComponent(type)}`)
00138|     return data
00139|   }
00140| 
00141|   return //...
00142| }
00143| ```
00144| 
00145| ### Creating tags from external data
00146| 
00147| You can use the data returned from an async function to tag the cache entry.
00148| 
00149| ```tsx filename="app/components/bookings.tsx" switcher
00150| import { cacheTag } from 'next/cache'
00151| 
00152| interface BookingsProps {
00153|   type: string
00154| }
00155| 
00156| export async function Bookings({ type = 'haircut' }: BookingsProps) {
00157|   async function getBookingsData() {
00158|     'use cache'
00159|     const data = await fetch(`/api/bookings?type=${encodeURIComponent(type)}`)
00160|     cacheTag('bookings-data', data.id)
00161|     return data
00162|   }
00163|   return //...
00164| }
00165| ```
00166| 
00167| ```jsx filename="app/components/bookings.js" switcher
00168| import { cacheTag } from 'next/cache'
00169| 
00170| export async function Bookings({ type = 'haircut' }) {
00171|   async function getBookingsData() {
00172|     'use cache'
00173|     const data = await fetch(`/api/bookings?type=${encodeURIComponent(type)}`)
00174|     cacheTag('bookings-data', data.id)
00175|     return data
00176|   }
00177|   return //...
00178| }
00179| ```
00180| 
00181| ### Invalidating tagged cache
00182| 
00183| Using [`revalidateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag), you can invalidate the cache for a specific tag when needed:
00184| 
00185| ```tsx filename="app/actions.ts" switcher
00186| 'use server'
00187| 
00188| import { revalidateTag } from 'next/cache'
00189| 
00190| export async function updateBookings() {
00191|   await updateBookingData()
00192|   revalidateTag('bookings-data', 'max')
00193| }

00005| 
00006| `revalidateTag` allows you to invalidate cached data on-demand for a specific cache tag.

00017| 
00018| The revalidation behavior depends on whether you provide the second argument:
00019| 
00020| - **With `profile="max"` (recommended)**: The tag entry is marked as stale, and the next time a resource with that tag is visited, it will use stale-while-revalidate semantics. This means the stale content is served while fresh content is fetched in the background.
00021| - **With a custom cache life profile**: For advanced usage, you can specify any cache life profile that your application has defined, allowing for custom revalidation behaviors tailored to your specific caching requirements.
00022| - **Without the second argument (deprecated)**: The tag entry is expired immediately, and the next request to that resource will be a blocking revalidate/cache miss. This behavior is now deprecated, and you should either use `profile="max"` or migrate to [`updateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/updateTag).
00023|

This means calling `revalidateTag` will not immediately trigger many revalidations at once. The invalidation only happens when any page using that tag is next visited.

The recommended value is `"max"` which provides stale-while-revalidate semantics, or any of the other default or custom profiles defined in [`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheLife). Alternatively, you can pass an object with an `expire` property for custom expiration behavior.

00005| 
00006| > **Note:**
00007| > This API has been replaced by [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) in Next.js 16.

00010| `unstable_cache` allows you to cache the results of expensive operations, like database queries, and reuse them across multiple requests.
00011| 
00012| ```jsx
00013| import { getUser } from './data';
00014| import { unstable_cache } from 'next/cache';
00015| 
00016| const getCachedUser = unstable_cache(
00017|   async (id) => getUser(id),
00018|   ['my-app-user']
00019| );
00020| 
00021| export default async function Component({ userID }) {
00022|   const user = await getCachedUser(userID);
00023|   ...
00024| }
00025| ```
00026| 
00027| > **Good to know**:
00028| >
00029| > - Accessing uncached data sources such as `headers` or `cookies` inside a cache scope is not supported. If you need this data inside a cached function use `headers` outside of the cached function and pass the required uncached data in as an argument.
00030| > - This API uses Next.js' built-in cache to persist the result across requests and deployments. See [Caching and Revalidating](/docs/app/getting-started/caching).
00031| 
00032| ## Parameters
00033| 
00034| ```jsx
00035| const data = unstable_cache(fetchData, keyParts, options)()
00036| ```
00037| 
00038| - `fetchData`: This is an asynchronous function that fetches the data you want to cache. It must be a function that returns a `Promise`.
00039| - `keyParts`: This is an extra array of keys that further adds identification to the cache. By default, `unstable_cache` already uses the arguments and the stringified version of your function as the cache key. It is optional in most cases; the only time you need to use it is when you use external variables without passing them as parameters. However, it is important to add closures used within the function if you do not pass them as parameters.
00040| - `options`: This is an object that controls how the cache behaves. It can contain the following properties:
00041|   - `tags`: An array of tags that can be used to control cache invalidation. Next.js will not use this to uniquely identify the function.
00042|   - `revalidate`: The number of seconds after which the cache should be revalidated. Omit or pass `false` to cache indefinitely or until matching `revalidateTag()` or `revalidatePath()` methods are called.
00043| 
00044| ## Returns
00045| 
00046| `unstable_cache` returns a function that when invoked, returns a Promise that resolves to the cached data. If the data is not in the cache, the provided function will be invoked, and its result will be cached and returned.
00047| 
00048| ## Example
00049| 
00050| ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher
00051| import { unstable_cache } from 'next/cache'
00052| 
00053| export default async function Page({
00054|   params,
00055| }: {
00056|   params: Promise<{ userId: string }>
00057| }) {
00058|   const { userId } = await params
00059|   const getCachedUser = unstable_cache(
00060|     async () => {
00061|       return { id: userId }
00062|     },
00063|     [userId], // add the user ID to the cache key
00064|     {
00065|       tags: ['users'],
00066|       revalidate: 60,
00067|     }
00068|   )
00069| 
00070|   //...
00071| }
00072| ```

00075| import { unstable_cache } from 'next/cache';
00076| 
00077| export default async function Page({ params } }) {
00078|   const { userId } = await params
00079|   const getCachedUser = unstable_cache(
00080|     async () => {
00081|       return { id: userId };
00082|     },

00084|     {
00085|       tags: ["users"],
00086|       revalidate: 60,
00087|     }
00088|   );
00089|

00092| ```

You can mutate data in Next.js using [React Server Functions](https://react.dev/reference/rsc/server-functions). This page will go through how you can [create](#creating-server-functions) and [invoke](#invoking-server-functions) Server Functions.

## What are Server Functions?

A **Server Function** is an asynchronous function that runs on the server. You can call them from the client through a network request, which is why they must be asynchronous.

In an `action` or mutation context, they are also called **Server Actions**.

title: Mutating Data
description: Learn how to mutate data using Server Functions and Server Actions in Next.js.

You can mutate data in Next.js using [React Server Functions](https://react.dev/reference/rsc/server-functions). This page will go through how you can [create](#creating-server-functions) and [invoke](#invoking-server-functions) Server Functions.

## What are Server Functions?

A **Server Function** is an asynchronous function that runs on the server. You can call them from the client through a network request, which is why they must be asynchronous.

In an `action` or mutation context, they are also called **Server Actions**.

00024| [`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife) controls how long cached data remains valid. Use it inside a [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) scope to set the cache lifetime.
00025| 
00026| ```tsx filename="app/lib/data.ts" highlight={1,4,5}
00027| import { cacheLife } from 'next/cache'
00028| 
00029| export async function getProducts() {

00031|   cacheLife('hours')

00038| | Profile   | `stale` | `revalidate` | `expire` |

00044| | `days`    | 5m      | 1d           | 1w       |
00045| | `weeks`   | 5m      | 1w           | 30d      |
00046| | `max`     | 5m      | 30d          | 1y       |

00050| ```tsx highlight={2-6}
00051| 'use cache'

00053|   stale: 3600, // 1 hour until considered stale
00054|   revalidate: 7200, // 2 hours until revalidated
00055|   expire: 86400, // 1 day until expired
00056| })
00057| ```

Short-lived caches are automatically excluded from prerenders and become dynamic holes instead. See [Prerendering behavior](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife#prerendering-behavior) for details.

00061| See the [`cacheLife` API reference](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife) for all profiles and custom configuration options.
00062| 
00063| ## `cacheTag`
00064| 
00065| [`cacheTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheTag) lets you tag cached data so it can be invalidated on-demand. Use it inside a [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) scope:
00066| 
00067| ```tsx filename="app/lib/data.ts" switcher
00068| import { cacheTag } from 'next/cache'
00069| 
00070| export async function getProducts() {
00071|   'use cache'
00072|   cacheTag('products')

00075| ```
00076|

00096| import { revalidateTag } from 'next/cache'
00097| 
00098| export async function updateUser(id: string) {

00102| ```
00103| 
00104| ```jsx filename="app/lib/actions.js" highlight={1,5} switcher
00105| import { revalidateTag } from 'next/cache'
00106| 
00107| export async function updateUser(id) {
00108|   // Mutate data

00117| See the [`revalidateTag` API reference](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag) to learn more.
00118| 
00119| ## `updateTag`
00120| 
00121| `updateTag` immediately expires cached data for read-your-own-writes scenarios — the user sees their change right away instead of stale content. Unlike `revalidateTag`, it can only be used in [Server Actions](/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data).

00123| ```tsx filename="app/lib/actions.ts" highlight={1,12} switcher
00124| import { updateTag } from 'next/cache'
00125| import { redirect } from 'next/navigation'
00126| 
00127| export async function createPost(formData: FormData) {

00129|     data: {
00130|       title: formData.get('title'),
00131|       content: formData.get('content'),
00132|     },
00133|   })

00137| }
00138| ```
00139| 
00140| ```jsx filename="app/lib/actions.js" highlight={1,12} switcher
00141| import { updateTag } from 'next/cache'
00142| import { redirect } from 'next/navigation'
00143| 
00144| export async function createPost(formData) {
00145|   const post = await db.post.create({
00146|     data: {
00147|       title: formData.get('title'),
00148|       content: formData.get('content'),
00149|     },
00150|   })
00151|

00154| }

00166| 
00167| `revalidatePath` invalidates all cached data for a specific route path. Use it when you want to revalidate a route without knowing which tags are associated with it.

00171| 
00172| export async function updateUser(id: string) {
00173|   // Mutate data
00174|   revalidatePath('/profile')
00175| }
00176| ```
00177| 
00178| ```jsx filename="app/lib/actions.js" highlight={1,5} switcher
00179| import { revalidatePath } from 'next/cache'
00180| 
00181| export async function updateUser(id) {
00182|   // Mutate data
00183|   revalidatePath('/profile')
00184| }
00185| ```
00186| 
00187| > **Good to know**: Prefer tag-based revalidation (`revalidateTag`/`updateTag`) over path-based when possible — it's more precise and avoids over-invalidating.
00188| 
00189| See the [`revalidatePath` API reference](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidatePath) to learn more.
00190| 
00191| ## What should I cache?
00192| 
00193| Cache data that doesn't depend on [runtime data](/docs/app/getting-started/caching#working-with-runtime-apis) and that you're OK serving from cache for a period of time. Use `use cache` with `cacheLife` to describe that behavior.

title: Revalidating
description: Learn how to revalidate cached data using time-based and on-demand strategies.

> This page covers revalidation with [Cache Components](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents), enabled by setting [`cacheComponents: true`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) in your `next.config.ts` file. If you're not using Cache Components, see the [Caching and Revalidating (Previous Model)](/docs/app/guides/caching-without-cache-components) guide.

Revalidation is the process of updating cached data. It lets you keep serving fast, cached responses while ensuring content stays fresh. There are two strategies:

- **Time-based revalidation**: Automatically refresh cached data after a set duration using [`cacheLife`](#cachelife).
- **On-demand revalidation**: Manually invalidate cached data after a mutation using [`revalidateTag`](#revalidatetag), [`updateTag`](#updatetag), or [`revalidatePath`](#revalidatepath).

00104| ```jsx filename="app/lib/actions.js" highlight={1,5} switcher
00105| import { revalidateTag } from 'next/cache'
00106| 
00107| export async function updateUser(id) {
00108|   // Mutate data
00109|   revalidateTag('user', 'max') // Recommended: stale-while-revalidate
00110| }
00111| ```
00112| 
00113| You can reuse the same tag in multiple functions to revalidate them all at once. Call `revalidateTag` in a [Server Action](/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data) or [Route Handler](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route).
00114| 
00115| > **Good to know:** The second argument sets how long stale content can be served while fresh content generates in the background. Once it expires, subsequent requests block until fresh content is ready. Using `'max'` gives the longest stale window.
00116| 
00117| See the [`revalidateTag` API reference](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag) to learn more.
00118| 
00119| ## `updateTag`
00120| 
00121| `updateTag` immediately expires cached data for read-your-own-writes scenarios — the user sees their change right away instead of stale content. Unlike `revalidateTag`, it can only be used in [Server Actions](/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data).
00122| 
00123| ```tsx filename="app/lib/actions.ts" highlight={1,12} switcher
00124| import { updateTag } from 'next/cache'
00125| import { redirect } from 'next/navigation'
00126| 
00127| export async function createPost(formData: FormData) {
00128|   const post = await db.post.create({
00129|     data: {
00130|       title: formData.get('title'),
00131|       content: formData.get('content'),
00132|     },
00133|   })
00134| 
00135|   updateTag('posts')
00136|   redirect(`/posts/${post.id}`)
00137| }
00138| ```
00139| 
00140| ```jsx filename="app/lib/actions.js" highlight={1,12} switcher
00141| import { updateTag } from 'next/cache'
00142| import { redirect } from 'next/navigation'
00143| 
00144| export async function createPost(formData) {
00145|   const post = await db.post.create({
00146|     data: {
00147|       title: formData.get('title'),
00148|       content: formData.get('content'),
00149|     },
00150|   })
00151| 
00152|   updateTag('posts')
00153|   redirect(`/posts/${post.id}`)
00154| }
00155| ```
00156| 
00157| |              | `updateTag`                                   | `revalidateTag`                      |
00158| | ------------ | --------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ |
00159| | **Where**    | Server Actions only                           | Server Actions and Route Handlers    |
00160| | **Behavior** | Immediately expires cache                     | Stale-while-revalidate               |
00161| | **Use case** | Read-your-own-writes (user sees their change) | Background refresh (slight delay OK) |
00162| 
00163| See the [`updateTag` API reference](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/updateTag) to learn more.
00164| 
00165| ## `revalidatePath`
00166| 
00167| `revalidatePath` invalidates all cached data for a specific route path. Use it when you want to revalidate a route without knowing which tags are associated with it.
00168| 
00169| ```tsx filename="app/lib/actions.ts" highlight={1,5} switcher
00170| import { revalidatePath } from 'next/cache'
00171| 
00172| export async function updateUser(id: string) {
00173|   // Mutate data
00174|   revalidatePath('/profile')
00175| }
00176| ```
00177| 
00178| ```jsx filename="app/lib/actions.js" highlight={1,5} switcher
00179| import { revalidatePath } from 'next/cache'
00180| 
00181| export async function updateUser(id) {
00182|   // Mutate data
00183|   revalidatePath('/profile')
00184| }
00185| ```
00186| 
00187| > **Good to know**: Prefer tag-based revalidation (`revalidateTag`/`updateTag`) over path-based when possible — it's more precise and avoids over-invalidating.
00188| 
00189| See the [`revalidatePath` API reference](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidatePath) to learn more.
00190| 
00191| ## What should I cache?
00192| 
00193| Cache data that doesn't depend on [runtime data](/docs/app/getting-started/caching#working-with-runtime-apis) and that you're OK serving from cache for a period of time. Use `use cache` with `cacheLife` to describe that behavior.
00194| 
00195| For content management systems with update mechanisms, use tags with longer cache durations and rely on `revalidateTag` to refresh content when it actually changes, rather than expiring the cache preemptively.
00196| 
00197| > **Good to know:** In serverless environments, in-memory cache entries may not persist across revalidations. See [runtime caching considerations](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache#runtime-caching-considerations) for details.
00198|

title: Revalidating
description: Learn how to revalidate cached data using time-based and on-demand strategies.
related:
  title: API Reference
  description: Learn more about the APIs mentioned on this page.
  links:
    - app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife
    - app/api-reference/functions/cacheTag
    - app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag
    - app/api-reference/functions/updateTag
    - app/api-reference/functions/revalidatePath
---

> This page covers revalidation with [Cache Components](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents), enabled by setting [`cacheComponents: true`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) in your `next.config.ts` file. If you're not using Cache Components, see the [Caching and Revalidating (Previous Model)](/docs/app/guides/caching-without-cache-components) guide.

Revalidation is the process of updating cached data. It lets you keep serving fast, cached responses while ensuring content stays fresh. There are two strategies:

- **Time-based revalidation**: Automatically refresh cached data after a set duration using [`cacheLife`](#cachelife).
- **On-demand revalidation**: Manually invalidate cached data after a mutation using [`revalidateTag`](#revalidatetag), [`updateTag`](#updatetag), or [`revalidatePath`](#revalidatepath).

title: use cache
description: Learn how to use the "use cache" directive to cache data in your Next.js application.

The `use cache` directive allows you to mark a route, React component, or a function as cacheable. It can be used at the top of a file to indicate that all exports in the file should be cached, or inline at the top of a function or component to cache the return value. Functions and components that use `use cache` must be async.

> **Good to know:**
>

---
title: use cache
description: Learn how to use the "use cache" directive to cache data in your Next.js application.
related:
  title: Related
  description: View related API references.
  links:
    - app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-private
    - app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents
    - app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheLife
    - app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheHandlers
    - app/api-reference/functions/cacheTag
    - app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife
    - app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag
---

The `use cache` directive allows you to mark a route, React component, or a function as cacheable. It can be used at the top of a file to indicate that all exports in the file should be cached, or inline at the top of a function or component to cache the return value. Functions and components that use `use cache` must be async.

> **Good to know:**
>

The `cacheLife` function is used to set the cache lifetime of a function or component. It should be used alongside the [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) directive, and within the scope of the function or component.

## Usage

To use `cacheLife`, first enable the [`cacheComponents` flag](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) in your `next.config.js` file:
